takeaways: Eaton sells the electrical gear that keeps data centers and the grid running, and that business is on fire: sales up 28% to a record $8.95 billion, 19% of it organic, above the top of its own guidance.
Orders are the real story. Rolling 12-month organic orders rose 39% in Electrical Americas, 51% in Electrical Global and 20% in Aerospace, and backlog grew 46% in Electrical.
Segment margins hit a record 25.3%, above the high end of guidance.
It raised the full-year organic growth outlook to 13-15% and guided full-year adjusted EPS to $13.70-13.80, above the $13.60 consensus.
It also agreed to buy COL Group to add European capacity for data center and utility power distribution.
verdict: Eaton is the shovel seller of the AI gold rush, and the shovels are back-ordered. Record sales, record margins, record backlog. The only bear case is that everyone already knows this, which is why the stock had dipped into the print.
